## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Nissaggiya Pācittiya 29, titled *Sāsaṅka*, is an ecclesiastical rule belonging to the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule provides that a monk who stores any of his three robes in an inhabited area for more than six days incurs an offense of expiation involving forfeiture (*nissaggiya pācittiya*), obliging him to relinquish the robe and confess the transgression [SuttaCentral]. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].

The rule is widely attested across multiple early Buddhist Vinaya lineages. SuttaCentral notes full parallels in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* and *Parivāra*, as well as in the monastic codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan translations [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral also identifies an internal passage-level parallel in Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pāṭidesanīya 4 (Bu-Vb Pd4) [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus confirms this internal relationship, detecting an identical shared passage with Bu-Vb Pd4 (§2.5–2.11 ↔ §3.1.1–3.1.6 with 1.0 similarity) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records substantial Pali text-reuse with the *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha*, adjacent robe-related training rules (notably Nissaggiya Pācittiyas 2, 3, 14, 21, 23, 24, and 28), several Khandhaka chapters (Kd 15, Kd 16, Kd 18), and Vinaya commentaries and sub-commentaries such as the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi* and *Vinayavinicchayaṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, cross-linguistic alignments link passages of the text to Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* fragments and Tibetan translations, including the *Vinayasūtraṭīkā* (D4120) and the *Vinaya-uttaragrantha* (D0007) [DharmaNexus].
